text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chief of the international High Representative's office in Mostar Sir Martin Garrod urges joint Moslem-Croat police force resume its patrols amid reports of explosions and shooting in the Moslem-controlled part of the city.

- Moslem co-chairman of Bosnian Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, meets delegation from German car producer Volkswagen to discuss possibilities of renewed partnership between the Germans and their pre-war partner, Sarajevo Car Factory (TAS).

- The head of the Bosnian Trade Unions Association, Sulejman Hrle, says Moslem-Croat Federation prime minister Edhem Bicakcic should engage in a dialogue with unions on welfare issues to ensure social peace.

- Total number of expelled Moslem families from Croat- controlled part of Mostar during the last week was 28, out of which 23 returned to their homes with help from international police monitors and NATO-led Stabilisation Force. Five families did not want to return.

- Moslem co-chairman in Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, says that process of privatisation should not begin until proper economic regulations are adopted. But Edhem Bicakcic, prime minister of Moslem-Croat Federation, says privatisation laws should be adopted immediately.

- "Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation must not be punished for the things that Bosnian Serb entity does not want to do," Bicakcic says, referring to delay of international donors' conference for Bosnia.

- Croatian government suspends insurance payments for Bosnian embassy in Zagreb. Zagreb government says it doesn't have the money. The Bosnian embassy has been receiving telephone threats this week that the embassy building will be blown up, Bosnian Ambassador to Croatia Kasim Trnka says.
